_doc: Purpose: drafting-standard profile for the DIN (Germany) system, consumed by cadcore.i18n.standards (projection angle plus sheet/line/lettering/title-block conventions). Background: standard-dependent values must live in data rather than code branches, and any field whose standard text was not obtained stays null and is listed in na_fields, so 'not fetched' can never masquerade as a real value; no standard text is reproduced here (R3).

standard_numbers: DIN ISO 128-3 (number as cited by the evidence page; not independently verified against a DIN register)
source.retrieval_method: read-only fetch of public web pages (HTTP status recorded per URL); standard bodies are paywalled and none of their text is copied into this file

projection_angle_evidence.publisher: TU Darmstadt, Institute for Machine Elements and Machine Design (public German technical university tutorial)
projection_angle_evidence.shows: States that the two projection methods come from DIN ISO 128-3 and that the usual method for display in Germany and most European countries is projection method 1, i.e. first-angle; method 3 is described as the method usually applied in the USA (paraphrase).
projection_angle_evidence.grade: public university teaching source explicitly citing the DIN standard, paraphrased

projection_angle_evidence.publisher: IDEA Technology (Japanese engineering firm), JIS drawing-standards article series
projection_angle_evidence.shows: Independent public source listing Germany and France among the countries using the first-angle method (paraphrase). The server answered with HTTP 500 while still serving the article, so this URL is treated as low-grade corroboration only, never as the sole basis for a value.

source.na_policy: null means not fetched (-1), never 'zero'; every null field is listed in na_fields, and no unverified field is given a guessed value.
notes: na_fields lists exactly the null-valued fields, in contract order: a gate can assert set(na_fields) == {k for k, v in profile.items() if v is None}.

decimal_separator stays null on purpose even though German locale text uses a comma: this profile is drawing-standard data, and the locale-derived separator belongs to the i18n catalog / format layer, not to a value invented here.

DIN is largely harmonised with ISO for sheets and lettering, so ISO and DIN values are expected to converge later; until the bodies are read, both profiles keep the same unverified fields null rather than copying one set into the other.
